# YouTube Migration

The Awtsmoos lets a creator carry chronology, descriptions, captions, playlists, and source truth without counterfeit history;
Awtsmoos.com keeps every migration dry-first, resumable, provenance-aware, and published through the same native social current.

## Choose the right path

Use `/youtube/` for the authenticated YouTube manager, `/youtube/migrate/` for advanced archive tooling, and `/social/migrate/` for the unified social migration studio.

## Whole-channel archive

Use Google Takeout, deselect unrelated products, select YouTube and YouTube Music, choose the wanted data, create a one-time ZIP export, and download every generated archive part. Keep videos beside metadata/info JSON, descriptions, thumbnails, subtitles/automatic captions, and playlist metadata when supplied. Then open `/youtube/migrate/` and review the dry plan before publication.

Google Takeout help: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/3024190?hl=en
Google Takeout: https://takeout.google.com/

## One owned video

Use YouTube Studio → Content → the owned video menu → Download. Preserve description, thumbnail, caption, and playlist context you need beside the media, then use `/youtube/migrate/` when normalizing it into Awtsmoos creator/publication state.

YouTube Studio help: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/56100?hl=en
YouTube Studio: https://studio.youtube.com/

## Advanced creator migration

The advanced migration studio may generate creator-owned `yt-dlp` commands instead of pretending the browser can fetch everything. Prefer metadata-rich runs that preserve descriptions, thumbnails, subtitles, automatic captions, timestamps, playlist membership, and info JSON. Review every generated command before running it on a trusted machine and migrate only material you own or are authorized to migrate.

A typical flow is: identify the owned channel/playlist/videos; generate the command; download media and metadata; preserve thumbnails/captions/playlists; return the local archive evidence; generate and review a dry publication plan; upload required media; re-plan with returned public asset paths; publish idempotently through the unified social publication endpoint.

## Playlist, chronology, captions, and archives

YouTube playlists map to Awtsmoos Series only when source evidence supports that relationship. Preserve playlist provenance rather than fabricating membership. Use the original known publication timestamp when supplied; otherwise keep it unknown rather than coercing it to January 1, 1970. Preserve available subtitle/automatic-caption files, languages, descriptions, and source-supplied chapter-like metadata.

When `/youtube/migrate/` offers an Archive.org command workflow, treat it as an explicit advanced path. Review identifiers, metadata, and generated commands, and preserve resulting archive identifiers/URLs where supported.

## Dry planning and resumability

Planning must not publish. The migration API produces deterministic publication plans and idempotency keys; actual creation goes through `/api/social/unified-social/publish`. Long migrations should checkpoint completed keys, uploaded public asset paths, destination choices, and failures. Retry only unfinished work so re-planning cannot create duplicate posts.
